correctness.rationale: Digit induction yields a strictly positive carry gap for all \(p\ge2\) and \(1<lpha<2\). This establishes a bijective ordered parametrization; tuple splitting proves the exact ordered representation product and two moment formulas. Divisibility classes yield gap frequencies with a tail bounded by \(p^{-J}\); digit errors bounded by \(O(\log X)\) give density \(1/lpha\); iid digits give the stated CLT for \(p\ge3\). The covering order follows from explicit missing integers and a complete interval induction; sparse-order exponents use matching coefficient-count bounds. The executable verified 48,780 finite gaps, 1,760 directly enumerated fibers, and 20 finite complete-prefix cases. These computations corroborate but do not replace the proof.

The present unified claim adds exact full critical digit-gap frequencies, natural density, all ordered representation fibers, collision energies, Gaussian logarithmic fluctuations and the sharp general-base covering order. value.rationale: The full arithmetic of repeated sumsets of this published Cantor-type integer family is a motivated target. Determining all critical gaps with frequencies, densities, every ordered representation fiber, exact collision moments, and logarithmic fluctuation laws identifies meaningful additive structure unavailable from mere inclusion or finite examples. The sharp minimum additive covering order classifies every integer base and every real parameter and exposes a sparse-to-dense-to-complete transition. These are natural invariants, not arbitrarily chosen parameters; their exact answers may inform further additive-representation and energy studies. The claim does not purport to solve all orders \(h\) or eventual-cofiniteness questions.
